title: Brutalist Web
content: Apply brutalist web aesthetic with raw, exposed design. Black and white primary palette. System fonts and monospace typography. Visible borders and structural elements. No rounded corners - harsh geometry. Raw HTML aesthetic. Unconventional layouts breaking conventions. Include intentional ugliness and discomfort. Link underlines and default styling references. Challenging, honest, anti-design atmosphere.

variants.simple: Create raw brutalist web design with exposed structure, harsh typography, and anti-design aesthetic.
variants.detailed: Apply brutalist web aesthetic with raw, exposed design. Black and white primary palette. System fonts and monospace typography. Visible borders and structural elements. No rounded corners - harsh geometry. Raw HTML aesthetic. Unconventional layouts breaking conventions. Include intentional ugliness and discomfort. Link underlines and default styling references. Challenging, honest, anti-design atmosphere.
variants.advanced: Apply brutalist web aesthetic with raw, honest, challenging design. Philosophy: reject polish and convention, embrace raw functionality, challenge beauty standards in design. Color: primarily black (#000) and white (#fff), occasional raw accent (pure red #ff0000, blue #0000ff). Minimal color, maximum contrast. Typography: system fonts (Arial, Times, Georgia), monospace (Courier), deliberately unglamorous. Large, bold, sometimes uncomfortably large text. Visible HTML: design suggests raw markup - visible borders, default blue links with underlines, bullet points, horizontal rules. Structure exposed: grid lines visible, borders on everything, no hidden frameworks. Layout: intentionally unconventional - overlapping elements, unusual proportions, breaking the grid deliberately. No rounded corners: border-radius: 0 everywhere, harsh rectangles. Anti-decoration: no icons, no illustrations, minimal images - content is king. Hover states: can be jarring (color inversion, harsh changes). Scrolling: long scrolling pages, no slick interactions, functional scrollbars. Forms: default styling, no fancy inputs. Cursor: default cursor, no fancy pointers. Table layouts: reference to old-school table-based layout (ironically). Uncomfortable: design may feel wrong but is intentional. Text-heavy: large blocks of text, raw information display. Interactive: minimal JavaScript, progressive enhancement. Performance: fast by default - no heavy assets. Implementation: minimal CSS, embrace defaults, remove rather than add. Accessibility: despite harsh appearance, should be highly accessible - semantic HTML, high contrast, clear focus states, no motion issues.
